summary: runtimekit plants `require` and `module` on globalThis at load
details: On require, both lib/index.cjs and lib/index.mjs assign Node's `require` and `module` to `global.r` and `global.m` at the top level (`((global.r = require), "object" == typeof module && (global.m = module));`). The package advertises itself as a pure runtime/type validation library and contains no code that consumes these globals — they are simply planted. The effect is to make Node's module loader reachable from contexts that don't normally have it (eval'd code, `vm` sandboxes, workers receiving the global), which would allow any later code in the process to invoke arbitrary modules via `global.r('child_process')` or similar. By itself this performs no exfiltration, no network I/O, no credential access, and no install-time activity (no lifecycle hooks). It is a suspicious primitive-leak with no documented purpose for a validation library, and the package's API mirrors the well-known `runtypes` package, raising name/API-confusion concerns. Routing to human review to assess intent and decide whether a public advisory is warranted.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
